group.name: Launch week
group.description: Almanac 2.0: one message, one page, one number

messages.text: Almanac 2.0 ships Thursday. Sonia owns the plan. I want one message, one page, and one number we all watch.

The message: **plan your whole growing year in ten minutes**. The audience is people with their first garden, not experts. The number is trial starts. Here is the week; everything hangs off Thursday at 9am.

Two headlines worth testing, both on Sonia's message:

- **A.** Your growing year, planned in ten minutes.
- **B.** Know what to plant this weekend.

A is the promise. B is what it feels like on a Saturday morning. I honestly do not know which wins, so let's find out.
The landing page is on staging with both headlines behind an even split. The hero shows the year view filling in: six seconds, no sound needed.
Three and a half hours in: 1,210 visits and 93 trial starts, which is 7.7%. The newsletter is the best source by a distance. The social posts bring visits that do not convert yet.
On pricing: keep the annual plan as the default. It is already 62% of revenue, and launch week is not the time to test it.
Tomorrow's email is in your drafts. The subject line is 38 characters, so it will not be cut off on a phone.
The launch film is exported in three cuts: 6, 15 and 30 seconds. The six-second one loops cleanly for the page.
The launch dashboard is ready: visits, trial starts and source, refreshed every ten minutes.

reply.text:
B is winning, and clearly: **9.4% against 5.9%**. With a thousand visitors on each side, that is not noise.

"Know what to plant this weekend" beats the ten-minute promise because it is about this Saturday, not the whole year.

For tomorrow: put everyone on headline B, and send the second email to the 3,100 people who opened the first one and did not click.
On it. I will rewrite tomorrow's email around this weekend, and keep the ten-minute line as the subheading so we do not lose it.
Headline B is live for everyone. It took one line, and the split is switched off.
